detailed_review.score_reasoning: Baseline 10 - (F1 1 + F2 2 + F3 1 + F4 0.5 + F5 0.5 + F6 0.5 + F7 0.5 + F8 0.5 + F9 0.5) = 3.0, floored to 3. After the fix pass, open penalty is F9 0.5 + F10 0.5 = 1.0, giving 9.0, floored to 9 and capped at 9 regardless because remaining[] and further_improvements are non-empty. Delta +6. Two judgements drive the baseline number and both deserve stating plainly. F2 is scored high, at 2, because the abstract promises a Mac and a Windows PC and the prerequisites section answered the eligibility question for only one of them: reader consequence, not presentation, is the test, and a Windows reader would have learned their machine was too small only after downloading a build and being refused. F1 is scored medium rather than high because although the entry point was genuinely absent, the corpus routes almost every reader here through Getting started, which carries it. A baseline of 3 reads as FAIL on the verdict table and that would be a misleading headline on its own: the shape of this page was already right. Pass 0 came back completely clean, which is the finding that matters most on a page that was just reshaped. The declared `type: how-to` matches what every section does, the page is not two types at once, and no section the how-to shape requires is missing. All eight baseline deductions were concentrated in the Windows half of the prerequisites, one routing gap, and five small defects. The distance from 3 to 9 is mostly one section.
detailed_review.what_worked: The reshape held. Graded against wiki/page-types.md:96-127, the page now has an abstract that states the outcome, a prerequisites section that names only what later steps use, action-title sections one per task, and numbered steps in imperative mood inside each. Bold is used for UI controls and only for UI controls (**Open**, **Where Hearth installs**, **Download**, **Settings > Connection**, **Start**), code voice for identifiers and paths, and result notes follow their actions rather than replacing them. There is not a Step N heading or a noun label anywhere. On the governing principle of the recommended spine, the page holds: it branches by platform in exactly the three places the platforms genuinely differ (requirements, first open, install layout), each branch is two short H3s or a scoped heading rather than a parallel procedure, and sections 4 through 6 and 8 through 11 are written once. It reads as one guide, not two stapled together. All seven salvage passages landed and landed intact. The macOS first-open procedure is three steps with the remembering note as a result note (passage 1). The refusal is absorbed as prose with no figures, per the ruling, and it is better than its source: it adds the two facts the blockquote omitted, that the refusal comes after the scan and that the reason is memory rather than disk (passage 2). The Backend and Mind and voice rows are present, with a sentence explaining what the Mind and voice row reports (passage 3). The uninstall carries the copy-out-of-home warning, correctly promoted to Important because it is a data-loss consequence inside a procedure rather than a requirement duplicated from a prerequisites list (passage 4). All five log filenames and all four failure modes are present, written as a term list, which is both the correct container under the style guide and the reason two bold-lead warnings did not come across (passage 5). The Windows install root prose and its fenced tree are present, the prose split sensibly between the default-location subsection and the tree (passage 6). The four-tier dictionary paragraph is present and tightened (passage 7). Of the changed[] items, F2 is the one that changes what the page can do: a Windows reader can now answer the question the section exists to answer. F3 is the one that matters most per word, because it turns a data-loss warning that pointed at a folder the page said did not exist into one that names a folder that does. F1 gives the page a first move. On the two specific questions the dispatch asked: the `## What comes next` link points at Meeting your persona, which exists, is a how-to, and was written in this same phase, so the ruling is satisfied and no reader is sent to the decision record. And `metal` in lowercase code voice does read correctly to a reader comparing the page against their screen: desktop-client/src/components/setup/SetupFlow.tsx:499 renders plan.backend with no transform and crates/hearth-probe/src/machine.rs:288 sets it to the lowercase string, so the page matches the screen character for character, and code voice is the right signal that the value is a literal rather than a proper noun. The author's deviation was correct and printing `Metal` would have been the error.
detailed_review.what_holds_score_down: Two open items, one point between them. F9: the uninstall procedure's fourth step is macOS-only, so a Windows reader who works the list deletes the install root and still has the application installed, with nothing telling them whether they are finished. Nothing in the tree or the corpus states the Windows removal step, so it is blocked on research rather than guessed at. F10: the sentence saying Hearth compares what it needs against your free disk and warns you when the space is not there sits only in the macOS subsection, although crates/hearth-probe/src/plan.rs:236-243 makes it platform-neutral. That one is my own doing, introduced on regrade as a consequence of writing the Windows requirements without repeating a sentence F5 had just flagged as duplicated. Beyond the scored items, three things are open on the page and none of them is chargeable against it. The 17,408-token context window cannot be settled from this tree, because it depends on the exact byte count a real machine reports through a crate this repository does not vendor, and the dispatch rules it out as a defect the author introduced; it is correct for the m1-air-8gb fixture. The absence of a Windows first-open procedure is deliberate and belongs to T10. And wiki/clients/macos.md:97-108 will carry a second copy of the right-click-Open steps until T6 runs. One further item is worth flagging outward rather than downward: the two Windows video memory figures now on this page are correct for real graphics cards, but the thresholds they approximate are 4,466,165,856 and 5,432,533,497 bytes, which read as 4.47 GB and 5.43 GB decimally and as 4.16 GiB and 5.06 GiB in the units the product's own human() uses. The sibling page states them decimally. Real cards ship in powers of two, so a 4 GB card is refused and a 6 GB card coexists under either reading and no reader is misled today, but the two pages and the product are not using one basis and that is a corpus-level thing to settle rather than an installing.md defect.
